hacker_news.title: Tell HN: Google Search to start locking down search behind a login wall
hacker_news.description: Usually, when I used Google Search on some ISP CGNAT IP addresses (not even a VPN), I usually get countless CAPTCHAs evertime I initiate a new session to Google Search on a new private browsing window (probably an artifact from residential proxy botnets). Recently, in addition to that, they started to just lock the entire search results page behind a login prompt on some of those bad IP addresses (like YouTube does for some time with the "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" prompt). This potentially makes the service less accessible, especially for those using a shared/public computers. I did not even get this prompt on some VPN IPs, and even no CAPTCHAs at all, even with a free one like given by Firefox. Has anyone encountered that? I just encountered this today. It's really unfortunate for the internet to become less friendly to signed-out users, especially since AI scrapers starting to "abuse" the internet for their value.

hacker_news.title: Show HN: Isometric SF – A pixel-art map of the SF Bay Area
hacker_news.description: Technical Write-up: https://www.justinchavez.com/blog/isometric-sf-how/ Hi HN! Showcasing this fun project. I took 1300 square miles of the SF Bay Area from Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles and transformed them into a cohesive pixel map. It's really fun to explore and stumble upon various famous landmarks like Apple Park, Palace of Fine Arts, or UC Berkeley. The technicals involve using Nano Banana 2 to train a Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 LoRA which is used to prototype the style and generation methods. For final map I used Qwen to train a Klein 4B LoRA which reproduced the style at 1/4 of the cost. More details in the blog post. Let me know what you think! I really enjoyed this process of fine-tuning smaller open source models. If I did the map with Nano Banana 2 it would have cost around 7k USD! Credit for the idea goes to Isometric NYC.
